## Answer

In `flash_firmware` (`src/agentic_hil/tools.py`, lines ~296–306), when `self.backend.flash_firmware(...)` raises an exception, the method drops the bench's remembered symbol ELF outright:

```python
try:
    result = self.backend.flash_firmware(staged["artifact"], reset_after_flash)
except BaseException:
    self._symbol_elf = None
    raise
finally:
    self.artifacts.release_stage(staged["artifact"])
```

The reasoning, per the inline comment, is that a backend which raised may have contacted or partially written the target, so the previously-remembered ELF can no longer be trusted to describe whatever is now on the board. Since `_remember_symbol_elf` (also in `tools.py`, ~line 314) only runs on a *returned* result — never on a raised exception — this exception handler is the only place that clears `self._symbol_elf` for a raising backend call. It sets `self._symbol_elf = None` and then re-raises the exception unchanged, so the coordination wrapper still reports the failure/effect as unknown, but a subsequent ST-Link symbol dump (via `offline_symbol_info` in `src/agentic_hil/backends/gdbdebug.py`) will get the `symbol_source_not_available` refusal rather than resolving a symbol against a build the failed flash may have replaced.

The docstring on `_remember_symbol_elf` clarifies the contrast: only a *returned* result that proves the flash never started (`side_effect_status == "not_started"`) is allowed to keep the old remembered ELF; any raised exception is treated even more conservatively — the source is dropped unconditionally, since there's no side-effect status to consult at all.
